name: Denisa Qosja
intro: I work at the intersection of machine learning and signal analysis, developing methods that help us extract more information from radar and remote sensing data.
bio: As a research scientist at Fraunhofer FHR, my work spans target detection and recognition, complex-valued neural networks, and generative models for signal enhancement and synthetic SAR imagery. My projects also explore semantic segmentation of Sentinel-2 satellite images.

headline: Radar Signal Processing and AI Engineer
about: I am a Radar Signal Processing and AI Engineer with over four years of experience in applied research at Fraunhofer FHR, focusing on combining signal processing and machine learning to advance radar sensing and AI-based perception. A large part of my research has focused on detecting and characterizing small targets in challenging environments, working with various radar data representations, including high-resolution range profiles (HRRP), range–Doppler maps, and micro-Doppler spectrograms.

Another important focus has been addressing the limited availability of labeled radar data through synthetic data generation, particularly using generative models to improve target recognition and model generalization. I am also interested in multimodal learning, combining the complementary strengths of radar and optical sensors to develop more robust perception systems across varying environmental conditions.
